description_short.value: Lomé-based holding company of the Ecobank group, a pan-African bank with banking subsidiaries in 32 African countries, serving corporate, commercial and retail customers.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Ecobank Group Annual Report 2025 (report of the directors: legal and regulatory framework, principal activity)

description_full.value: Ecobank Transnational Incorporated (ETI) is the parent company of the Ecobank group. It was incorporated in Lomé, Togo, on 3 October 1985, under a private-sector initiative led by the Federation of West African Chambers of Commerce and Industry and ECOWAS. A headquarters agreement with the Republic of Togo gives it certain immunities and tax exemptions, and the WAMU Banking Commission supervises it as a financial holding company. Its business is owning and acquiring the operating banks: at the end of 2025 the group had banking operations in 32 African countries, a licensed bank in Paris, and representative offices in Addis Ababa, Beijing, Dubai, Johannesburg and London. It organises them in two business segments, Corporate and Investment Banking and Consumer and Commercial Banking, and four regions: Francophone West Africa (UEMOA), Nigeria, Anglophone West Africa (AWA) and Central, Eastern and Southern Africa (CESA). Its Ghanaian subsidiary, Ecobank Ghana, is separately listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange as EGH. The group reports serving about 30 million customers, and in September 2025 it sold Ecobank Mozambique to FDH Bank. ETI's shares have been listed since 2006 on the Ghana Stock Exchange, the Nigerian Exchange and the BRVM in Abidjan, with most shares held on the Nigerian register. In December 2025 Nedbank sold its 21.22% stake to Bosquet Investments. At the end of 2025 the largest shareholders were Bosquet Investments (21.22%), Qatar National Bank (20.10%), Arise B.V. (14.10%) and South Africa's Government Employees Pension Fund (13.72%). ETI reports in US dollars, with a financial year ending 31 December.
